request.spec:
Each user can choose which columns of the people list their screen shows: a checkbox per column
(claimed, due-total, statement-count, stated-total, statement-date, overdue-count, overdue-total,
patrons, backing, hold, retired, terms, contact, aliases), per user's screen. A column switched off has no cell on the screen at all; totals, the header, the summary and every other figure are
unaffected.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Each user can choose which columns of the people list their screen shows: a checkbox per column
(claimed, due-total, statement-count, stated-total, statement-date, overdue-count, overdue-total,
patrons, backing, hold, retired, terms, contact, aliases), per user's screen. A column switched off has no cell on the screen at all; totals, the header, the summary and every other figure are
unaffected.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each user can now pick which people-list columns their screen shows. Two of the four tests pass under `bin/e2e`. The other two (scenarios 2 and 3) fail, and the cause is a mistake in the test itself, not the app.

**Why the two tests fail:** at lines 700, 793, 1078 and 1166 the spec expects the parent sheet field (`sheet-parent`) to show the literal text `"__SHEET__-p"`. That's a placeholder the test generator never filled in. The test sets the parent to `` `${sheet}-p` ``, and its own audit check at line 756 expects that real value. The app correctly shows the real sheet id, so these assertions can't pass unless the app showed a fake value. I didn't do that and didn't edit the spec. On a scratch copy of the spec with only those four lines corrected to `` `${sheet}-p` ``, all four tests passed; I then deleted the copy. The spec needs fixing at those four lines.

**What I built (front end only):**
- **The checkboxes:** `features/people/columns.slot.tsx` adds a `column-<id>` checkbox for each column. The list includes `excess`: the spec switches it off even though the request doesn't name it.
- **Where the choice is kept:** a `hideColumns` setting in the page address (URL), handled in `features/people/columns.ts`. That's how the app keeps other per-screen choices like "show retired", so it is per user's screen and survives reloading a sheet. Nothing is stored on the server and nothing is written to the audit file.
- **Hiding cells:** each person-row component checks the setting and leaves out its cell when the column is off.
  - Claimed, due-total, excess, overdue-count, overdue-total, terms and contact lose the whole table cell.
  - Hold, retired, the three statement figures, patrons, backing and aliases share a cell with action buttons (hold, retire, add alias and so on). For those only the value and its label disappear, so the actions still work.
- Totals, the header and the summaries are unchanged.

**Port clash:** when I first ran `bin/e2e`, all four tests failed within seconds. The app hadn't started because port 3000 was taken by other runs on this machine, so the tests were hitting a different server. The results above come from `PORT=3091 bin/e2e`.
